demos.title: Shared cursors
demos.blurb: Every tab sees the other cursors move, and a fresh tab knows where they all are before anyone moves again.
demos.details: Cursor positions live in an ephemeral map subscription — no history, entries expire by TTL. A client that joins gets the full snapshot from the subscription itself, so there is no REST call to load initial state and no gap to bridge.

demos.title: Limited inventory shop
demos.blurb: Two tabs buy the last item at the same moment. One wins, the other retries with fresh stock.
demos.details: Each purchase is a compare-and-swap write: the client reads current stock, decrements it, and writes back only if nothing changed in between. Conflicts auto-retry, and the snapshot stays correct in every tab.

demos.title: Sprint board on PostgreSQL
demos.blurb: Drag a card between columns — the board update and the real-time message commit in the same transaction.
demos.details: The PostgreSQL map broker stores state in regular SQL tables, so a write and its publication either both land or both roll back. No dual write, no outbox to babysit.

demos.title: Live polls
demos.blurb: A vote lands in PostgreSQL and shows up in every open tab as part of the same commit.
demos.details: Each vote atomically updates the result row and publishes the change. Late joiners get the current tally from the subscription, so counts never drift between tabs.

demos.title: Sync protocol visualizer
demos.blurb: The three phases of a map subscription, frame by frame: paginated state, stream catch-up, live updates.
demos.details: Disconnect and re-subscribe on demand and watch how the client converges — either catching up from the stream or re-syncing from scratch. Useful for seeing what the SDK hides.

demos.title: Game lobby
demos.blurb: Players join and leave, the sidebar keeps up, and a reconnecting client lands on the same list as everyone else.
demos.details: Presence built on map subscriptions in recoverable mode — a reconnecting client catches up from the stream instead of re-fetching the whole participant list.

demos.title: 100,000 presence members
demos.blurb: Two tabs subscribed to one presence channel while the population fills to 100k. Each cell is a connection.
demos.details: Green flashes are joins, red are leaves. The tabs connect during the fill, so they reconcile a moving target: paginated state plus live joins. The clip ends with a reconnect — state paginates back at 10k entries per page. This is a deliberately extreme shape, not a recommended one.

demos.title: Drone tracking over San Francisco
demos.blurb: 500 drones move over a map, and each client only receives the ones inside its own viewport.
demos.details: Cell-based spatial partitioning with shared poll subscriptions: the viewport decides which keys a client tracks, and the tracked set changes as the map is dragged. Per-key authorization is signed by the backend.

demos.title: Football scoreboard
demos.blurb: Live match state for a page full of games, with a counter showing how much delta compression saves.
demos.details: Deltas are computed per key, between successive values of the same entry, so a client receives a compact patch when only the score changes instead of the full payload.

demos.title: Vote counts in a feed
demos.blurb: Counters update only for the posts currently on screen — scrolling changes what the client tracks.
demos.details: One shared poll subscription covers the whole feed. The client declares the keys it cares about, the server polls them together, and results arrive in one stream instead of a subscription per post.

demos.title: Real-time leaderboard
demos.blurb: Ranks move as scores change, with rows highlighting on the way up and down.
demos.details: Redis holds the leaderboard, Python triggers ranking changes, React renders. Uses cache recovery and versioned publications so a reconnecting client never shows a stale board.

demos.title: Stock ticker with server-side filtering
demos.blurb: One channel carries every ticker, and the client asks for AAPL only. The rest never leaves the server.
demos.details: Publications carry tags, and a subscription can attach a filter over them. Filtering happens on the server, so clients save bandwidth and CPU without extra channels to manage.

demos.title: Kitchen orders
demos.blurb: One orders table shared by all restaurants, one channel per restaurant, each display sees only its own.
demos.details: The PostgreSQL stream broker turns rows into publications, so the order state and the notification stay consistent without a separate message bus.

demos.title: Loki logs in the browser
demos.blurb: Type a LogQL selector, get a live tail of matching logs over WebSocket.
demos.details: A gRPC subscription stream proxy sits between Centrifugo and Loki: the browser speaks WebSocket, the backend speaks gRPC, and each subscription becomes its own server-side stream.

demos.title: Grand chat tutorial app
demos.blurb: A multi-room messenger with unread counters, room discovery, and state that survives a reload.
demos.details: The full tutorial app: Django backend, React frontend, Centrifugo in front. Built to go past the usual chat basics — message ordering, catch-up after a gap, and per-room counters that stay right.

demos.title: Push when the tab is closed
demos.blurb: The same chat sends a web push notification once the user is no longer connected.
demos.details: Centrifugo PRO tracks who is online and delivers a push notification to devices that are not. One place decides between a real-time message and a push.

demos.title: The same chat at 100k connections
demos.blurb: The tutorial app with a hundred thousand connections attached, still delivering messages as usual.
demos.details: Same code, more load: Redis engine, several Centrifugo nodes, and a load test that keeps 100k WebSocket connections subscribed while messages flow.

demos.title: Two million particles
demos.blurb: A physics simulation streamed to the browser as binary frames, rendered in real time.
demos.details: A Go simulation publishes particle state through Centrifugo at high frequency. Started as a port of David Gerrells' experiment and turned into a test of how much binary data a single connection can take.

demos.title: Streaming LLM responses
demos.blurb: Tokens appear as the model generates them, delivered over a temporary channel instead of a direct SSE pipe.
demos.details: The backend calls the model and publishes tokens to Centrifugo. The browser subscribes to a per-generation channel, so the stream survives a reload and can be watched from more than one tab.

demos.title: AI stream that survives a disconnect
demos.blurb: Drop the connection mid-generation: the client reconnects and the missed tokens arrive at once.
demos.details: Token streams get history and recovery like any other channel. The playground also shows publisher-side aggregation, transport switching, and a second tab picking up the same generation.

demos.title: RabbitX exchange
demos.blurb: A perpetual futures exchange running Centrifugo for order books, trades, and account updates.
demos.details: RabbitX pushes market data to traders through Centrifugo. Their team wrote about the setup, including how they handle bursts and keep clients in sync during volatile periods.
